Korea’s Bae Jun-ho struck late as it came from behind to snatch a 2-1 victory over China on Wednesday and reach a record fourth successive Asian Games final in men’s soccer.</p>
<p class="p3">The defending champion will bid for an unprecedented fourth straight gold medal in Saturday’s final at Toyota stadium against familiar foe Japan, who beat Uzbekistan, 9-8, on penalties after the match was locked at 1-1 at the end of extra time.</p>
<p class="p3"><span class="s1">Another South Korean gold would bring its players an exemption from the country’s compulsory military service for adult males as Asian Games champion.</span></p>
<p class="p3">The Koreans have stand-in captain Eom Ji-sung to thank for reaching the final as he set up goals for Bae and Lee Young-jun.</p><div id='div-gpt-ad-AD1-783716' data-csco-ad-base='AD1' style='text-align:center;'></div>
<p class="p3"><span class="s1">Bae volleyed home in the 82<sup>nd</sup> minute from next to the far post after latching onto a long, lofted cross from Eom, who stepped up to replace injured skipper Lee Gi-hyuk.</span></p>
<p class="p3">Bae said he and Eom had plotted the winning goal at halftime when the game was level at 1-1.</p>
<p class="p3">“I knew he was going to go for the far post and that’s why I ran behind the left back,” Bae told Reuters.</p>
<p class="p3">“He called to me and then I scored. Beautiful pass, it was really easy to score.”</p><div id='div-gpt-ad-AD2-783716' data-csco-ad-base='AD2' style='text-align:center;'></div>
<p class="p3">Lee headed in Eom’s corner after 33 minutes to cancel out China forward Wang Yudong’s opening strike.</p>
<p class="p4"><b>CHINESE REGRET<br />
</b>China bowed out from its first Games semifinals in 28 years with some regret, having gone one step further as Under-23 Asian Cup runner-up in January.</p>
